title: Novel quadridentate salen type triple-decker sandwich ytterbium complexes with near infrared luminescence

synthesis.procedure: H2L was prepared according to reported procedures. Yellow crystals of 1 suitable for single-crystal X-ray diffraction were grown by slowly diffusing a MeOH solution (15 mL) of Yb(OAc)3·4H2O (0.0422 g, 0.1 mmol) into a CH2Cl2 solution (15 mL) of H2L (0.0633 g, 0.2 mmol).
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow diffusion of a MeOH solution of Yb(OAc)3·4H2O into a CH2Cl2 solution of H2L afforded yellow single crystals.

properties.summary: NIR Yb(III) luminescence is observed upon ligand-centered excitation at 335 nm, with emissions near 974–975 nm assigned to 2F5/2 → 2F7/2 plus crystal-field/Stark bands at 1003 and 1033 nm. Ligand-to-metal energy transfer is efficient. Intensity is stronger than for 2 and stronger in MeCN than MeOH. Time-resolved NIR decays were fit to two components (τ1 = 2.339 μs, 54.97%; τ2 = 10.56 μs, 45.03%). UV-vis absorption maxima were reported in MeOH.

synthesis.procedure: A MeOH solution (5 mL) of Yb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.0467 g, 0.1 mmol) was added to a CH2Cl2 solution (25 mL) of H2L (0.0633 g, 0.2 mmol). The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 24 h, changing from yellow to dark yellow. Hexane or petroleum ether (60–90 °C) was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature. Yellow single crystals of 2 were harvested in two weeks. Complex 2 could also be obtained by addition of Yb(NO3)3·6H2O to complex 1.
synthesis.time: stirred 24 h; crystals harvested in two weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by slow diffusion crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Hexane or petroleum ether (60–90 °C) was slowly diffused into the filtrate at room temperature; yellow single crystals formed in two weeks.

properties.summary: NIR Yb(III) luminescence is observed upon excitation at 335 nm, with emissions near 974–975 nm (2F5/2 → 2F7/2) and additional bands at 1003 and 1033 nm. Intensity is weaker than for 1, attributed to exposed bidentate nitrate ligands. Time-resolved NIR decays were fit to two components (τ1 = 1.566 μs, 49.38%; τ2 = 8.75 μs, 50.62%). UV-vis absorption maxima were reported in MeOH.
